narr: After strong to severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds and flash flooding across southeast California during the afternoon and evening of August 31st, upper level dynamic support along with abundant moisture remained favorable for isolated showers and thunderstorms to continue and produce locally heavy rainfall across parts of southwest and south-central Arizona during the early morning hours on the 1st. The heavy rainfall resulted in increased flow in Tiger Wash, impacting downstream low water crossings. No damage or injuries were reported.
ev: A Maricopa County Flood Control District stream gage along Tiger Wash exceeded alarm stage, impacting downstream low water crossings on Eagle Eye Road. Timing of impacts to Eagle Eye Road were estimated to be 65 minutes after the stream gage exceeded alarm stage. No damage or injuries were reported.
lsr: A MARICOPA COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT STREAM GAUGE ON TIGER WASH EXCEEDED ALARM STAGE AT 232 AM CREATING A FLOODING PROBLEM ON EAGLE EYE ROAD DOWNSTREAM AN ESTIMATED 65 MINUTES LATER.
